question: At a UK roundabout, which traffic must you give way to?
options: Traffic approaching from your immediate right
explain: Rule 185: To give way to traffic approaching from your right.

question: When is it safe to enter a roundabout?
options: When there is a safe gap so circulating traffic does not have to slow down
Whenever you reach the line first
Whenever the car in front enters, without looking
Only after stopping for three seconds
explain: Rule 185: Entering only when there is a safe gap to the right.

question: If a car on the roundabout is signalling left to take the exit before yours. What should you do?
options: Wait until you see it actually start turning off
Flash your lights to hurry it up
explain: Rule 185: Not to rely on another driver's signal alone before pulling out.

question: What should you also watch for before entering a roundabout besides cars?
options: Cyclists, motorcyclists, and pedestrians crossing the exit
explain: Highway Code Rule 185 reminds drivers to watch out for cyclists, riders, and pedestrians.

question: What road marking sits across each entrance to a roundabout?
explain: Highway Code Rule 185 marks roundabout entrances with broken give-way lines.

question: When approaching a roundabout, which side should you look to first for circulating traffic?
explain: Rule 185: To give way to traffic coming from your right.

question: Does an entering car have priority over a car already on the roundabout?
options: No, traffic already on the roundabout from the right has priority
explain: Highway Code Rule 185 gives priority to circulating traffic from the right.

question: What should you do if a car is. Already on the roundabout to your right and close?
options: Stop behind the give-way line and wait for a safe gap
Accelerate hard in front of it
explain: Rule 185: Waiting until there is a safe gap.

question: Why should you also glance left and ahead as you pull onto a roundabout?
options: Traffic ahead may stop suddenly or a pedestrian may cross
Nothing can be ahead of you
explain: Highway Code Rule 185 checks both circulating traffic from the right and hazards ahead.

question: At a mini-roundabout, does the same give-way-to-the-right rule apply?
options: Yes, give way to traffic from your right just like a full roundabout
Traffic from the left goes first
explain: Highway Code Rule 185 and 188 apply the same give-way-to-the-right rule at mini-roundabouts.

question: If the roundabout is completely clear to your right, must you still stop?
options: No, keep moving smoothly if it is safe and clear
Yes, stop for three seconds every time
explain: Rule 185: Giving way, not stopping unnecessarily when the way is clear.

question: At a mini-roundabout, three cars arrive at once and nobody has clear priority. What should you do?
options: Make eye contact, proceed slowly, and give way if unsure
explain: Highway Code Rule 185 and courtesy advice help resolve deadlocks safely.

question: A lorry on the roundabout is taking the next exit. Blocking your view of the lane behind it. What should you do?
options: Wait until the lorry clears so you can see any hidden vehicles behind it
explain: Rule 185: Not to enter when a large vehicle hides traffic to your right.

question: Why must you watch the outer lane carefully when joining a two-lane roundabout?
options: A driver in the inner lane might switch outward or a cyclist might be riding there
The outer lane is always closed
explain: Rule 185: Watching all circulating lanes and cyclists before entering.
